'''Henrik Julius Ager-Hanssen''' (21 July 1930 – 19 November 2004) was a Norwegian nuclear physicist and businessperson. He spent his career in the nuclear energy sector from 1956 to 1975, then in the petroleum company [[Statoil]] from 1976 to 1998.

==Career==
He was born in [[Stavanger]], and after education at the [[University of Oslo]], [[Catholic University of Leuven (1834–1968)|University of Leuven]] and [[New York University]] he got the degree Master of Nuclear Engineering. He taught nuclear energy technology at the New York University from 1956 to 1957, and then spent many years as a researcher, research leader and director at the [[Institute for Energy Technology]]. He spent his four last years in nuclear energy as chief executive of [[Scandpower]] from 1971 to 1975.<ref name=ntb>{{cite news|title=Henrik Ager-Hanssen 60 år 21. juli|agency=Norwegian News Agency|date=4 July 1990|language=Norwegian}}</ref>

In 1976 Ager-Hanssen was hired as vice chief executive of the petroleum company [[Statoil]], based in his hometown Stavanger.<ref name=ntb/> He was reportedly headhunted by [[Finn Lied]].<ref name=obit1>{{cite news|title=Henrik Ager-Hanssen er død|work=Stavanger Aftenblad|date=23 November 2004|language=Norwegian|page=27}}</ref> In 1988 he briefly served as the acting chief executive, following the retirement of [[Arve Johnsen]].<ref>{{cite news|title="En vandrer på jorden" forlater Statoil|date=14 January 1988|language=Norwegian|agency=Norwegian News Agency}}</ref> From autumn 1989 he was a special adviser in the company, with special responsibility for its [[Brussels]] branch. In 1998 he founded his own consulting firm Ager Energy Management.<ref name=obit1/>

Internationally, Ager-Hanssen chaired the Committee for Special Studies and the Energy for Tomorrow's World Commission, both within the [[World Energy Council]].<ref name=ntb/> In 1994 he was named on the [[European Commission]]'s Consultative Forum on environmental policy, despite Norway not being an EU member.<ref>{{cite news|title=Henrik Ager-Hanssen skal fylle Delors visjoner|work=Dagens Næringsliv|author=Ask, Alf Ole|date=20 January 1994|page=11|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He has served as chair of [[Norsk Helikopter]], ''[[Stavanger Aftenblad]]'', [[Offshore Northern Seas|ONS]], EnTech Invest,<ref name=obit1/> [[:no:Scan Geophysical|Scan Geophysical]],<ref name=obit2/> [[:no:Kongsberg Våpenfabrikk|Kongsberg Våpenfabrikk]], the Institute for Energy Technology, the [[Center for International Climate and Environmental Research]] and [[Det Stavangerske Dampskibsselskab]].<ref name=ntb/> He has been a board member of [[Det Norske Veritas]],<ref name=obit2/> the Chr. Michelsen Institute and [[Siemens|Siemens Norway]].<ref name=ntb/>

He was an elected fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]], the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]], the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref name=ntb/>

==Personal life==
He married Bjørg Ager-Hanssen in 1958 and had two children, Marianne and [[Christen Ager-Hanssen]]. He died from cancer in November 2004.<ref name=obit1/><ref name=obit2>{{cite news|title=Henrik Ager-Hanssen|author=Røren, Eivald|authorlink=Eivald Røren|work=Aftenposten|date=8 December 2004|language=Norwegian}}</ref>
